notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 1 heading sits at a level the page never opens — "Native American - Wabanaki" is an h4 with no h3 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "For help sourcing Halal products, work with your local distributors" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Wabanaki Resources" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Additional Resources" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 1 heading is plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 2 links on this page open a file — 2 Video — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Give the sub-headings their rule
decisions.why: 3 sub-headings are plain bold text. The design has a treatment for them — a teal rule down the left and a line across — and it had never been used on any page, because it needs a wrapper an author would have to know about.

decisions.label: Jumbotron callouts become notes
decisions.why: 1 callout is built as a Bootstrap jumbotron, which the component list replaced with dc-note and which Bootstrap itself removed in version 5. Same content, the site's own callout.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 3 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 5 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Left-align a section header
decisions.why: 1 section header is centred, where 1,103 of the 1,139 on the site are left-aligned — the component list says not to centre them. The band runs the full width of the column, so a centred title has no fixed relationship to anything else, and a two-line one breaks the left edge every other heading shares. Only the alignment changes.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: For recipes and videos that were created with the help of Mihku Paul, artist, writer and Wabanaki culture consultant please visit Recipes and Videos from the Culinary Classroom

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 2 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.

decisions.label: Match the heading treatments to the final levels
decisions.why: 1 heading was wearing the wrong treatment for its level — a section header round a sub-heading or the reverse — because the wrapper was chosen before the outline was finished.
